clue.text: Soldiers infiltrating abbey get life

indicators.note: the soldiers get inside the abbey

parts.note: Bath Abbey, the great church in the English city of Bath

explanation.surface: Troops storm a famous abbey and somehow come out with a new lease of life.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbey is named by its city: Bath Abbey stands in Bath, a spa town in the west of England, so 'abbey' hands over BATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Breath is used for life itself, as in 'while there is breath in me'.

clue.text: Side of ribeye smothered in gravy — starter for lunch in City?

indicators.note: a side is an edge, so the first letter of ribeye

parts.note: Bisto is a leading British brand of gravy granules

indicators.note: the first letter, as a starter is the first course

explanation.surface: A menu note: a steak drowned in gravy, served as a lunchtime starter in a City restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: BISTO is a household name in Britain, a powdered gravy mix, and a gift to setters. The R goes in after the B, and the question mark flags 'City' as a real city, Bristol in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol is a city in south-west England.

clue.text: Senior wife divorced by one forming bond

parts.note: a welder joins metal, forming a bond

explanation.surface: An older wife is left by a husband who is busy forming a new bond elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' reads as marriage beside 'wife' and 'divorced'; here it is the metal joint a welder makes.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a senior person, and as an adjective elder means senior.

clue.text: Hiding in ancient city — not a task for revolutionary

indicators.note: the A is taken out of task

parts.note: the ancient city of the Trojan War

explanation.surface: A lost soul hiding in an old city decides a revolution is not a job for them.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is read out of order: the reduced TASK is what hides in Troy, placed just before the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon Trotsky was a leader of the Russian Revolution.

clue.text: Noise on the radio still

definitions.meaning: an adjective here: motionless, not moving

explanation.surface: Someone notices the radio has gone quiet, or is still crackling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like the adverb 'even now'; it is the adjective 'motionless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Static is radio crackle, and static also means stationary or still.

clue.text: The Royal Marines: the ultimate in peerless British units

indicators.note: the last letter of peerless

explanation.surface: A proud boast that the Royal Marines are the finest of all British military units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British units' looks like regiments; it means units of measurement. A therm is a unit of heat that British gas bills were long charged in.
explanation.definitionFit: The therm is a unit of heat energy used for British gas billing.

clue.text: Chasing rabbit's tail, biting foot of hare, I growl savagely and loudly

definitions.text: Chasing rabbit's tail, biting foot of hare, I growl savagely and loudly

indicators.note: the last letter of rabbit
I GROWL is rearranged in a wild fashion

parts.note: I GROWL rearranged; it opens between G and R to take the E

indicators.note: the bottom, so the last letter of hare

parts.note: last letter of hare, bitten into the jumble

explanation.surface: A hunting animal snarls as it runs down a rabbit and snaps at a hare.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a tiger wolf is the spotted hyena, a predator that does chase and bite prey while making a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger wolf is an old name for the spotted hyena, a loud and savage hunter of small game.

clue.text: Conservative politician wearing glasses has scheme on vacation to make notes

parts.note: two round lenses, drawn as OO
Member of Parliament, inside the OO

indicators.note: the word is emptied, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A bespectacled Tory MP has a plan to write things down while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make notes' suggests jotting in a notebook; the notes are musical, and a composer makes them.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose is to write music, which is to make notes.

clue.text: They remove caps from batsmen to sustain courage

indicators.note: in a down answer the batsmen hold up what sits above them

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
the two batsmen who start a cricket innings are the openers

explanation.surface: Cricketers take off their caps to find some courage.
explanation.walkthrough: The caps look like cricket caps; they are the metal caps on bottles. BOTTLE for courage is British slang ('he lost his bottle'), and the openers are the batsmen who go in first.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the caps are the metal crowns on bottles, which these gadgets lever off.

clue.text: Perhaps North's to achieve success with diamonds

explanation.surface: At the bridge table, the North player hopes to make the contract with diamonds as trumps.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the players are named North, South, East and West, so 'North' and 'diamonds' paint a card game. 'Perhaps' marks North as one example: a north wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by 'Perhaps': North names a direction a breeze can blow from.

clue.text: Man goes wild securing ace when playing well

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

indicators.note: to go wild is to lose all order, so the letters of MAN GOES run riot into a new arrangement

parts.note: MAN GOES rearranged, split after ON

explanation.surface: A player erupts with joy after serving an ace while in top form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ace' reads as a tennis serve in this sporting picture; it is the card that counts as one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on their game is performing at their best, playing well.

clue.text: Begins with small puddings

parts.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
tarts are puddings; pudding is British for dessert

explanation.surface: A meal opens with some little desserts.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'pudding' means any dessert course, so tarts qualify.
explanation.definitionFit: Starts and begins are the same verb in the same form.

clue.text: Also, stealing money not a pointer to the future

indicators.note: the A is dropped from ARROW

parts.note: ARROW, a pointer, without its A

explanation.surface: Pocketing cash is no guide to what lies ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a pointer' reads as 'no indication'; it instructs you to take A away from a pointer, an arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomorrow stands for the future generally, as in 'the world of tomorrow'.

clue.text: They provide regular services for the masses

definitions.text: They provide regular services for the masses

parts.note: not buses or utilities: church services held every week
not the general public: the Masses of the Catholic church

explanation.surface: A description of public utilities, like a bus company serving the general public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Services' sounds like buses or utilities and 'the masses' like the public; they are church services and the Masses celebrated there.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergymen hold regular church services, and priests say Masses.

clue.text: Left Italy in German translation

indicators.note: the letters are turned into a new form

parts.note: I = Italy, its international car code
taken as written, to be jumbled with the I

explanation.surface: Someone left Italy and has the phrase put into German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it places Italy inside German; it is simply two more letters in the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Remaining and left both mean still there after the rest has gone.

clue.text: Part of quiche Lorraine slice sent back

indicators.note: a slice cut from inside the words
the slice is returned, so read backwards

explanation.surface: A diner sends back a slice of quiche Lorraine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' looks like the hidden-word signal; 'Part' is the definition, and 'slice' does the hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the theatre: what an actor plays in a production is called either word.

clue.text: Party accepts 1,000,000 deposit

parts.note: DUP = Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A political party takes a million-pound donation.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is a Northern Irish political party, often in the news.
explanation.definitionFit: To dump something is to deposit or set it down carelessly.

clue.text: Argued about backing Democrat plot to imprison separatists once

indicators.note: the whole string is then read backwards

parts.note: ETA, the former Basque separatist group, now disbanded
a flower bed is a plot

explanation.surface: A news item: people argued over supporting a Democrat scheme to jail former separatists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' reads as a conspiracy; it is a garden bed. 'Once' marks ETA as a group that no longer exists. Assembled DETABED, then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To debate a question is to argue about it.

clue.text: US swimmer oversleeps if he's shattered

indicators.note: the word is turned over, so read backwards
IF HE'S is broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: An American swimmer sleeps in when he is exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oversleeps' must be split into 'over' and 'sleeps'; kip is British slang for sleep. 'Swimmer' is a fish, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: The spikefish is an American name for a spiny fish of the Atlantic, a swimmer.

clue.text: Making his mark in disputed region

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A leader stamps his authority on a contested territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' reads as a verb in a sentence about influence; its job is to build new letters from HIS MARK.
explanation.definitionFit: Kashmir is a region whose ownership is disputed by India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Documents civil service retiring with expensive cars

indicators.note: withdrawing, so going backwards

explanation.surface: A civil servant retires with paperwork and a garage of luxury cars.
explanation.walkthrough: A Rolls is a Rolls-Royce, the byword for an expensive car.
explanation.definitionFit: An old form of document: before bound books, records were written on long rolled sheets.

clue.text: Building is more cracked

indicators.note: the letters are built into a new word

explanation.surface: An old building is getting more and more cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' reads as a noun, a structure; it is the verb, constructing new letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimose is a botanical term for covered in cracks or fissures.

clue.text: Black cat chases ball catching 6 in limbo

indicators.note: the black cat runs after the ball, so comes behind it
the cat holds the 6 inside it

parts.note: a ball is round, like O

explanation.surface: A black cat plays with a ball of wool.
explanation.walkthrough: The '6' looks like a cross-reference to 6 down; it is just the number, written VI in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbo and oblivion are both states of being forgotten or neglected.

clue.text: Weapons and fruit onboard

explanation.surface: A ship's inventory: weapons and fruit stowed on board.
explanation.walkthrough: SS for steamship is how setters put things on board: the ship's two letters wrap around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the spear, a shaft with a pointed head, is among the oldest hand weapons.

clue.text: Delicate flower picked up by female? On the contrary

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted up means read upwards
swap the roles: the female goes inside the flower
held close by, here enclosing

parts.note: a flower is a river, the NILE; it reads upwards

explanation.surface: A fragile bloom is picked by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is something that flows, a river. 'On the contrary' flips the clue: the flower takes in the female, not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means small and delicate, like an elf.

clue.text: Messenger's very good memory about outing

indicators.note: about can mean around, as in 'scattered about the room'

parts.note: a trip is an outing, inside SO

explanation.surface: A messenger fondly remembers a special day out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very good' looks like praise; it splits into SO and G. A stripogram is a message delivered by a performer who strips.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripogram is a messenger who delivers a greeting while stripping.

clue.text: In New York, season top of fajitas with everything

indicators.note: the first letter of fajitas

explanation.surface: A New York diner serves fajitas loaded with all the toppings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In New York' tells you the answer is the American word: fall, for what British English calls autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Fall is the American name for autumn.

clue.text: Blade of green grass, damp after early rain, initially flourished

indicators.note: take the first letter of each word
the letters are waved about, as a sword is flourished

parts.words: green grass, damp after early rain, initially
parts.note: first letters of green, grass, damp, after, early, rain

explanation.surface: A lawn looks lush after a spring shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blade of green grass' reads as one blade of grass; 'Blade' alone is the definition. 'Flourished' seems to mean the grass thrived; a blade is flourished too.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a short stabbing knife is one kind of blade.

clue.text: Article describes hesitation in retreat, like in scenes of conflict

indicators.note: an army in retreat moves backwards, so the letters are read backwards
to describe a circle is to draw it

parts.note: ER, the hesitation sound, backwards, inside AN

explanation.surface: A news report describes hesitancy among forces pulling back, as happens in war zones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describes' looks like 'tells about'; in geometry, to describe a circle is to draw a line around something, which makes it a container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Arenas are places where contests or fights happen, scenes of conflict.
